chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Yazeed Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Husayn ibn Ayn (the brother of Malik ibn Ayn) who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the words a man says to another man: 'May Allah reward you with goodness (Khair)', what is meant by it? So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Khair' is a river in Paradise, its source is from Al-Kawthar, and Al-Kawthar's source is from the pillar of the Throne. Upon it are the dwellings of the Successors (peace be upon them) and their Shias. On the banks of that river are maids growing; every time one is taken, another grows in its place. It was named after that river, and that is His Exalted Statement: 'In them are goodly things (Khair), beautiful ones.' So when a man says to his companion: 'May Allah reward you with goodness (Khair)', he means by that those dwellings which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for His elite and the chosen ones from His creation.

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The Successors (Imams), who have dwellings on the river of Khair
key_terms.الْكَوْثَرِ: Al-Kawthar, the river in Paradise from which the river of Khair originates
key_terms.جَوَارِي: Maids (Houries) that grow on the banks of the river
key_terms.خَيْراً: Goodness; specifically a river in Paradise in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of saying 'Jazakallahu Khairan' in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'Khair' in the common greeting is elevated from a general blessing to a specific eschatological reference to the River of Khawthar, which flows from the base of the Divine Throne. The Imam links this river directly to the spiritual stations of the Imams and their Shias, interpreting the phrase as a prayer for the recipient to attain these exclusive high ranks in Paradise. This interpretation underscores the Shia theological emphasis on the centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt in the structure of the afterlife and the unique status of their followers.
